subject: Streamline — payment paths, bank credentials & PO tagging activation
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.o@streamlineinc.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Streamline — payment paths, bank credentials & PO tagging activation

Hi Liam —

Thanks for starting the vendor onboarding packet with us. To finish bank activation and wire/ACH routing so we can process the first PO, we need the following from you: 

- A signed bank authorization letter (can be a bank template) that includes account name, account number, routing number, and a statement authorizing ACH debits/credits to Redwood Inference.
- W9 (if not already provided).
- Preferred remittance metadata rules: how should we label PO number, invoice number, and line-level descriptors in the remittance feed/CSV? We can accept a structured remittance (CSV/EDI) or a simple free-text field; please indicate which you prefer and the exact field name(s).
- Whether you accept ACH only, wire fallback, and if you have a preferred receiving bank for urgent payments.

If you can attach the signed bank letter + W9 to a reply, we’ll route to Finance and schedule a test micro-deposit (expected within 24–48 hours) and provide a sample PO to align on invoice tagging.

Quick ask: can you indicate a point of contact on your side for any bank follow-ups (name, phone)?

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Chloe Martin
Procurement Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com
--
Attachment: (placeholder) onboarding_checklist.pdf (PDF, 45KB)

Hi Chloe —

Thanks — attaching what you asked for. See files below:

- Streamline_Bank_Authorization_2028.pdf (signed by our CFO) — contains account name, routing, account number and explicit authorization for ACH credits.
- Streamline_W9_2028.pdf — current on file.

On remittance fields: we operate best with structured remittance. Our preferred fields are: PO#: "po_number" (required), Invoice#: "invoice_id" (required), InvoiceDate: "invoice_date" (optional), LineDescription: "description" (optional). If you send a CSV, include headers exactly as above. For free-text remittance (PDF invoices), please ensure the PO# field is on the first page and clearly labeled "PO#".

We accept ACH by default; wire is available for expedited settlements (fees apply). Our treasury team prefers ACH to our primary account but will accept wire to the same account if Redwood requires same-day funds.

POC: Maeve Lin — Treasury Ops — maeve.lin@streamlineinc.com — +1 415-555-0182

Forwarded message included below for context.

Best,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Finance Operations
Streamline Inc.

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.o@streamlineinc.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 06 May 2028 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Streamline — payment paths, bank credentials & PO tagging activation

Hi Liam & Chloe —

Thanks for the docs and the clear remittance field spec, Liam — that helps a lot. A couple of quick items from Finance before we kick off the micro-deposit: 

1) Bank auth review: the authorization looks fine but we need a bank letter that explicitly states the account will accept ACH credits and includes a letterhead + bank contact. The attached PDF is acceptable; finance will request the bank contact name/phone if the bank letter does not contain it.

2) Structured remittance: we can ingest a CSV with headers exactly as you specified. Could you confirm whether the PO# is numeric-only or may include hyphens/alpha (e.g., "PO-12345" or "PO12345"). We prefer to map to a single field "po_number" and recommend using plain alphanumeric characters only.

3) Micro-deposit testing: we are planning a single micro-deposit (USD $0.12) from our test account tomorrow (05/07) in the morning PST. If you can confirm receipt and the exact settled amount we’ll mark the account active.

4) Could you attach a one-line sample invoice (CSV preferred) that matches your production formatting so we can validate parsing? I’ve attached a small example CSV we use internally — "po_mapping_example.csv" to show header expectations.

If all good we’ll move to activate the channel and create the PO template for your first scheduled payment run.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
--
Attachment: po_mapping_example.csv (CSV, 2KB)

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.o@streamlineinc.com>

Chloe / Jonas —

Confirmed — we received your notes. Responses inline: 

- Bank letter: the bank contact (Keiko Tanaka, VP Treasury Services, keiko.tanaka@banknorth.com, +1 212-555-0100) is included in the authorization PDF you received. If Finance needs a separate bank verification letter, we can request it but the attached authorization should satisfy standard processors.

- PO formatting: our PO numbers can include hyphens and alpha (e.g., "PO-2028-541"). We can provide a pre-production CSV that uses only alphanumeric if you prefer; otherwise we will keep the hyphen format and your parser will strip non-alphanumeric chars if necessary. Let us know which you prefer for the first month.

- Micro-deposit: Maeve confirmed she will watch for the test deposit and report the exact cents. We are ok with a single $0.12 test or a two-deposit verification — whatever Finance prefers.

- Attached: Micro-deposit-Confirmation.pdf (screenshot from our banking portal showing recent incoming test transfers) and a sample_invoice_streamline.csv that mirrors production.

We accept ACH as primary; wire is used only for exceptions. Our AP team is copied here (payments@streamlineinc.com) for visibility and to speed any follow-ups.

If you want us to change PO formatting for the onboarding month, say the word and we’ll provide both hyphen and no-hyphen samples.

Best,
Liam O'Connor
